# Review of SEEN-109, attempt 6, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned on opus with the task text of triage record 64 and two questions: whether
the path-comparison defect is closed as a class on both sides, and whether the
amendment to `route_rule` is sound and said the same way in all four places. It
read the ticket, all sixty-four records, the twenty files of the focus set, both
calibration report files, `harness/tests/test_kpi.py` and `CLAUDE.md`, and it
answered the first question by running fourteen path shapes through both
comparisons rather than by reading them.

Verdict: **return**, on F1.

**On the class.** Closed, on both sides, and checked by running it: plain, a
hunk, a line and column, a dot directory, a leading `./` on either side,
backslashes, surrounding whitespace, an absolute path, an unreadable tail, a
drive letter, a bare directory, a double slash, a `./` segment mid-path and a
case difference. On the triage side every one is either an escape or placed
nowhere; on the route side every one is either charged to a slice or held as
uncharged. The partition is exhaustive by construction rather than by patching:
`unchargeable` is the complement of the union of every slice's planned files.
The fifth review's own measurement reverses, from zero against zero and a
printed go-live to stay-shadow on both verdicts with the file named.

**On the amendment.** Sound, and verified rather than taken on trust: the
committed report counts nothing and every journal in the repository predates
`counted_from`, so it is still a rule written before the first number. The code,
`route_rule`, the workflow and the committed report agree. One observation
rather than a finding: the charging half can never change a verdict, because a
window holding an uncharged finding short-circuits to stay-shadow before the
rates are compared, so it shows only in the printed table.

## The findings

**F1, medium, `harness/kpi.py:455`.** A regression introduced by attempt 6's own
fix. Routing `kpi.findings` through `calibration.latest_findings` makes every
finding a returning round recorded count as waived, because a real return
carries `status: open` and only a passing advance carries `resolved`. Run
against this ticket's own journal it reports fixed 0, waived 8, while all eight
findings of notes 17, 25, 36, 46 and 56 were fixed. Before the change `waived`
was structurally unreachable, because the review gate refuses an advance finding
that is not resolved, so the change turns a dead figure into a systematically
wrong one. The one test for the fix builds its returning finding with the
helper's default `status: resolved`, a shape no return in this repository
carries, which is the fixture criticism the fifth review made of itself.

**F2, low, `harness/calibration.py:541`.** `verdict_routes` tests a group by its
rate rather than by its membership, so `no slice was routed below the strongest
tier` prints both when the downgraded group is empty and when it holds slices
carrying zero points. Both answers give the same safe verdict, which is why it
is low, but a founder auditing the report is told the group is empty when the
table above shows it is not.

**F3, low, the ticket file.** The Outcome names all four files, which is what
the fifth review asked for, and the counts written around them were not updated:
it still says the check fails on three files and lists four deviations while
enumerating six, and the ordinals no longer match.

**F4, low, `harness/calibration.py:622`.** `went_live_problem` swallows a
`HarnessError` from `journal.read` into an empty record list, so a damaged
journal and a go-live naming a record that was never written give the same
message and send a reader to fix the wrong thing.

## The deterministic checks it was handed

`red_before_green` holds for attempt 6 line for line: record 59's six failures
are the ones record 63 predicts. `tests_added` holds but for F1's own test.
`acceptance_entries` holds, matched one to one. `slice_files` fails on four
files, all four now named in the Outcome and all four forced by earlier reviews
or by the change propagating into fixtures; F3 is only about the counts written
around them. `pull_request` stays unavailable. Ground rules clean by codepoint.
`doctor` runs green with `calibration` in its checked list, and the committed
report is current: the reviewer regenerated it and found it byte-identical.

## What the shadow window will read from this round

The triage would have excluded 14 of 19 files, 57.89 per cent. F1 lands in
`harness/kpi.py` and F3 in the ticket file, both of which the narrowing would
have dropped, and both are below high, so by the ticket's own definition neither
is an escape. F2 and F4 are in `harness/calibration.py`, which the triage kept.
No escape; the ticket is excluded from the window by name in any case.
